# Logs declaration fixture

This source overlay composes the invented five-seat Comms fixture with Logs. It selects the existing base, Homes and Runtime bodies, then Comms, Logs and Host. It gives no Identity key and contains no recorded output or runtime secret.

```sh
bash tests/fixtures/logs-workplace/prepare.sh /absolute/new/config
```

The destination must be new and its parent must exist. Preparation delegates to comms-workplace/prepare.sh, copies the Logs body and its LOGS programs, and appends this fixture's record-reach lines to the inherited COMMS programs. It preserves the inherited mail/grab/write declarations. It copies source only and calls no reader, frame, carrier or model. No PLAN, BUILD, record file, chain, journal or home is materialized.

The workplace supplies pane kept and programs none, an explicit byte limit, the file sink and the relative record path records. File is chosen deliberately so the independent comparison does not depend on a host's user manager or leave journal entries. Harbor, Dock and two seats provide progressively scoped pane overrides. The record reach overlay starts from a workplace ban, adds an office grant, adds a room ban and then adds individual grants. Its purpose is to keep record selection and permission to read a record as separate declarations.

The Comms/Logs ruling of 2026-11-12T19:25Z settles formation and the frame's selection boundaries. Allowing access to a currently unrecorded target is legal and must show an empty read-only directory. No expected per-seat result, source freeze, native receipt or frame result has been published. Independent predictions belong outside this fixture and must be sealed before the first invocation.

For a later isolated rehearsal, supply the Comms fixture's documented support tree and the existing probe/seed helpers at their declared root-relative paths. Copy this fixture's root/records directory to records under that isolated workplace root as the record mountpoint; it contains no logs. Preparation does not supply a dummy replacement for those tools, initialize a journal or start a user service. See docs/logs.md for the formation and implementation boundary.
